content.text:
The latest issue is [#188 — “UX: Rebuild Inventory as an Icon Grid with Automatic Stacking and Fast Item Actions”](https://github.com/PJensen/jshack/issues/188), created November 14, 2026. It’s open, labeled `GAMEPLAY` and `PLAYER-ARC`, with no comments yet.

Its scope is a full player-inventory UX overhaul:

- Replace text rows with a responsive icon-tile grid using the existing item atlas.
- Preserve unidentified-item secrecy and provide safe icon fallbacks.
- Reuse and audit existing visual grouping and physical ECS stacking.
- Prevent loss of unique state: enchants, curses, durability, charges, sockets, unpaid status, scripts, etc.
- Add accurate quantity badges and safe backing-entity actions.
- Preserve Use, Equip, Apply/Socket, Identify, Throw, Drop, Pin, Set Spell, and pickup flows.
- Add predictable sorting, category filters, safe name search, and stable selection.
- Support mouse, touch, keyboard navigation, focus, filtering, and responsive layouts.
- Keep details/actions, weight, capacity, rarity, equipment, pins, and status indicators.
- Avoid changing ECS ownership, capacity rules, save/load, determinism, or item identities.

The implementation is divided into:

1. Audit current inventory behavior, icons, identification, grouping, stacking, and baseline tests.
2. Build the responsive grid, tile rendering, focus/navigation, and selection persistence.
3. Integrate stacking, sorting/filtering/search, quantity behavior, and action routing.
4. Polish responsive/accessibility behavior and add regression coverage.

The acceptance bar is explicitly high: genuine icon tiles, safe identification handling, correct stack semantics, no metadata destruction, preserved actions, keyboard/mouse/touch usability, mobile performance, and automated tests for grouping/stacking and navigation.
